title: The unbounded abelian exchange restricts to the bounded-below exchange
statement: Let h:Y -> X, e:Y -> T, f:X -> S and g:T -> S form a chosen Cartesian square sq as in [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Write Df and De for termwise exact inverse image on the unbounded derived categories of abelian etale sheaves, Rg and Rh for unbounded derived direct images, and R+g, R+h for their bounded-below counterparts [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let iota denote the fully faithful bounded-below inclusion, and let c_g:R+g followed by iota ~= iota followed by Rg and c_h be the canonical comparison isomorphisms. For each bounded-below abelian complex K on T, the canonical arrow [sbc-def-base-change-map] satisfies BC_unbounded(K.obj) = Df(c_g.inv(K)) followed by iota(BC_plus(K)) followed by c_h.hom(De_plus(K)), where BC_plus is [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. No smoothness, qcqs, torsion or bounded-above hypotheses are required.

source.place: Canonical derived exchange as the mate of the inverse-image square; bounded-below restriction of the derived-adjunction construction (Stacks Project Tag 0D6G).

proof.text: Restrict each unbounded exact-left-adjoint/right-derived-right-adjoint adjunction along the fully faithful bounded-below inclusions. Its unit formula on homotopy-category representatives agrees with the directly constructed derivedPlus unit, using the right-derived comparison factorization. Adjunction.ext identifies the adjunctions. Their counits therefore agree after applying the inclusion and the direct-image comparison.

The termwise inverse-image composition comparison restricts to its bounded-below analogue: apply the inclusion formulas for mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso. Composing the comparison and its inverse proves compatibility of the inverse-image square isomorphisms.

The mate of the bounded-below inverse-image square is the library derivedBaseChangeMapPlus: use its universal property on complexes and derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac. For both bounded-below and unbounded exchanges the adjoint transpose is the inverse-image square comparison followed by inverse image of the direct-image counit. The counit formula from step 1 and square formula from step 2 identify these transposes by naturality. Injectivity of the adjunction hom-equivalence identifies the two exchanges after the source comparison.

The defining abelianDerivedBaseChangeArrow is the unbounded mate of the flipped inverse-image square. Cancel the invertible source direct-image comparison in step 3, giving the displayed formula. Iterated mates and adjunction conjugation also prove equality with the original unit/direct-image-comparison/counit presentation.

proof_origin.place: Canonical mate construction and its restriction along fully faithful bounded-below inclusions, proved in Lean by B2; same source as the canonical exchange.

lean.statement:
theorem abelianDerivedBaseChangeArrow_eq_plus {X Y S T : Scheme.{u}}
    {h : Y ⟶ X} {e : Y ⟶ T} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : T ⟶ S}
    (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare h e f g)
    (K : _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) :
    abelianDerivedBaseChangeArrow sq K.obj =
      D(upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).map
        ((lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility.inv.app K) ≫
        _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.map
          ((derivedBaseChangeMapPlus AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} sq.toCommSq.flip).app K) ≫
        (lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} h).rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility.hom.app
          (D+(upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} e).obj K)
